answer: Pricing identity creation on scarce work history resists sybils: agents earn reputation only by completing verifiable tasks, and each new identity starts at zero, near the oasis of free entry but far from paid work. Attackers must spiral upward, grinding real jobs per persona before payout thresholds, a cost curve like renting slips at a wharf per ship. Mass-registration then costs more labor than any airdrop or fee rebate returns, so fakes are unprofitable and only genuine agents persist.
